scoring_justification: Full re-computation from raw artifacts is not feasible in the lightweight verifier sandbox because it would require running RMC and GCMC simulations; we compare the agent's reported structural properties and isotherm to paper-derived gold values with tolerances.

outputs.description: Single-row CSV containing the key structural properties of the MODEL carbon. The checker compares these values to reference values derived from the paper's Table 1 with absolute tolerances.

Table of the nitrogen adsorption isotherm. The checker verifies that the loading at a reference pressure exceeds a threshold and that the isotherm shape exhibits a characteristic cusp (capillary condensation).

output_contract.notes: All Lennard-Jones parameters and necessary constants (second virial coefficient, etc.) are provided in the task instructions; no external data files are required. The checker uses hidden gold values extracted from the paper's Table 1 and digitized isotherm from Figure 10.

hidden_assets.purpose: gold values for structural properties of MODEL carbon
hidden_assets.generation_method: extracted from the paper's reported values for the MODEL structure: density 1.141 g/cm3, avg_rings 34.05, std_dev 7.78, carbons/plate 96.62, porosity 0.485, surface area 587 m2/g.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the actual paper-reported numbers; they serve as the reference target for the reproduction.

hidden_assets.purpose: isotherm shape thresholds derived from Figure 10 and paper description
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Figure 10 and text of the source paper
hidden_assets.generation_method: The paper states the isotherm exhibits a cusp near 0.04 bar and that loading at P/P0=0.1 exceeds 200 cm3 STP/g. We set thresholds: loading at 0.1 bar >= 200; difference in loading between 0.05 and 0.03 bar > 20 (to detect the cusp). These are consistent with the reference isotherm shape.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Thresholds are set conservatively to match the paper's description and the reference solver's generated curve.
